newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's controversial tax-cut bills face vote.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's controversial tax-cut bills face vote.

text.p: Brazil's Chamber of Deputies is due to vote Wednesday on proposed priority treatment for controversial legislation that would exempt an estimated four million small Brazilian companies from tax, a deputy said.

If deputies vote in favor of priority treatment, the two bills -- which the government says would hurt revenues -- will be put to a vote in the lower house next week, said Dep. Augusto Nardes, who is leading a campaign for their approval.
Under the terms of the bills, small companies would be exempt from tax and employer contributions on turnover of up to 204,000 reais a year.
Government officials say the bill would cut tax revenues by about $4.0 billion a year, but Nardes put the impact at $1.8 billion.
"That's not much to pay when you consider there are four million small companies which could create an extra eight million jobs as a result of these bills," he said.
The legislation was drawn up by Sen. Jose Sarney, a former Brazilian president who currently presides over the Senate and has attacked the government on unemployment.

Sarney scored a victory over the government in July when the Senate's Economic Affairs Committee approved the two bills which, thanks to a loophole in congressional rules, did not have to be approved on the floor of the Senate.
The government is reported to be preparing a counter-proposal which would create a single tax for small companies with a 10 percent charge on turnover.
Nardes said he and groups representing small businesses would be prepared to negotiate the government's reported proposal, but felt the 10 percent rate was too high.
